span: and would lead to harm and unhappiness; thus, out of compassion, I am inclined to remain silent." This refers to how the noble Vajragarbha accepted the purity of that assembly, yet by saying "if hesitation and doubt were to arise after hearing," he shows the fault of not being a vessel for this teaching. Because two types of faults regarding a single object are present, he showed them as two: "hesitation" and "doubt." These two are inconsistent with straightforward action. It is "doubt" because there is suspicion in the mind and because it removes virtue by causing it to decline. Thus, he has fully shown the cause for not proceeding and the cause for turning back from proceeding. Then, for that very same reason, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra again requested the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha: "O Son of the Conqueror, please explain it well; by the power of the Tathagata, such inconceivable states as these will be perfectly protected and will also become objects of trust. Why is that? O Son of the Conqueror, this is the reality <note>original: "dharmata"</note> obtained when this explanation of the grounds is spoken: here, all Buddhas will turn their intention toward it, and all Bodhisattvas also strive to protect this very ground of wisdom. Why is that? O Son of the Conqueror, this is the primary practice, because it is for the sake of correctly accomplishing the Buddha-dharma. O Son of the Conqueror, it is like this: for example, that which precedes all syllables, letters, and the teaching of numbers is the alphabet <note>literally: "mother of letters"</note>, and that which brings them to completion is also the alphabet; whatever written letters, syllables, and teachings of numbers there are, none can be shown without the alphabet. O Son of the Conqueror, likewise, since all Buddha-dharma are accomplished through practice, those grounds are the precursor. Because they result in the culmination of the self-arisen primordial wisdom, they are the completion. Therefore, O Son of the Conqueror, speak, and the Tathagatas..."
head: However, if others were to hear such an inconceivable state as this, and having heard it, hesitation and doubt were to arise, it would be of no benefit to them for a long time
old_translation:
"It will lead to harm and unhappiness. Therefore, out of compassion for them, I prefer to remain silent." By saying this, the noble Vajragarbha acknowledged the purity of the current assembly, but by mentioning "if doubt and hesitation were to arise after hearing it," he showed the danger for those who are not suitable vessels for this teaching. 

Because two types of faults attach to a single object, it is shown in two ways: "doubt" and "hesitation." These two are inconsistent with straightforward action. It is "doubt" because there is suspicion in the mind, and "hesitation" because it clears away virtue by causing virtue to decline. In this way, he fully demonstrated the cause for not proceeding and the cause for turning back from proceeding. 

Then the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra again requested the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha for that very reason: "O Son of the Conqueror, please explain it well! By the power of the Tathagata, they will come to be well protected and to have trust even in such inconceivable states as these. Why is that? O Son of the Conqueror, when this explanation of the Grounds <term>bhumi</term> <gloss>the stages of a Bodhisattva's path</gloss> is taught, this is the attainment of the nature of reality. For in this, all Buddhas will turn their intention toward it, and all Bodhisattvas will also strive to protect this very ground of wisdom. Why is that? O Son of the Conqueror, this is the primary practice, for it is for the sake of perfectly accomplishing the Buddha-dharmas. 

O Son of the Conqueror, for example, that which precedes all syllables, letters, and the teaching of numbers is the alphabet <term>matrika</term> <gloss>the mother/matrix of letters</gloss>, and that which completes them is also the alphabet. Whatever written letters, syllables, and teachings of numbers exist, they cannot be taught without the alphabet. O Son of the Conqueror, likewise, since all Buddha-dharmas are accomplished through practice, the Grounds are what precede them. Since they lead to the limit of self-arisen wisdom, they are what bring them to completion. Therefore, O Son of the Conqueror, speak! The Tathagatas,"
